Monday 16 November 2026 · 23 stories
Morning Brief
Nifty 50 fell 0.61% to 25,144 and decliners led 1,597 to 972
Today’s read
The biggest names carried the session. The fifty most traded stocks returned +2.10% weighted by turnover, against -0.51% for the median stock, a gap of 2.6 percentage points, so most stocks did worse than the busiest names suggest.

Sharda Motor Industries Limited rose 8.1% on 109 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “Investor Presentation”.

Alicon Castalloy Limited rose 17.3% on 132 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about quarterly results, “Financial Result for quarter ended 30th September, 2026 is enclosed.”.

Automotive Axles Limited rose 10.1% on 123 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Bharat Semi raises $24 million in seed round led by Info Edge, South Park Common”.

Nothing in the news or in exchange filings explains the volume in BF Utilities Limited (248x), Dhanlaxmi Bank Limited (177x), ITI Limited (147x). That usually points to a sector story rather than a company one.

Management commentary on alternative pipeline bids in the GCC region will determine whether order intake can offset the shortfall.

US producer prices surged 6.5% year-on-year in October, signaling persistent wholesale cost pressures that delay monetary easing. High US interest rates narrow the sovereign yield spread with India, encouraging foreign institutional outflows and raising import costs via a weaker rupee. The upcoming US personal consumption expenditures data will confirm whether final consumer prices follow wholesale trends.

Higher terminal interest rates prolong elevated cost of capital, dampening loan expansion for retail lenders and weighing on discretionary demand for auto stocks. A sustained rise in the 10-year G-sec yield above 6.85% would confirm extended liquidity tightness.
